system: Tailwind CSS v4, semantic CSS-variable tokens mapped via @theme, toggled by a .dark class (not prefers-color-scheme).
rules: Theme colors only, compulsory, no exceptions: never use hardcoded Tailwind palette colors (text-blue-500, bg-red-500, border-gray-200, etc.), inline hex/rgb colors, or any other extra/arbitrary color not in the token list below, anywhere in generated UI — not even for a one-off accent, illustration, or 'just this one element'. Every color used must be one of the semantic tokens below.
Always use the semantic token classes below (bg-primary, text-foreground, border-border, ...) so generated UI automatically follows the consumer's theme in both light and dark mode.

Every base token except background/foreground/secondary/border/input/ring has a matching '-foreground' token for text/icons placed on top of it (e.g. bg-primary + text-primary-foreground, bg-destructive + text-destructive-foreground).

Page background: bg-background. Card surfaces: bg-card. A distinct section within a page (not the whole page, not a card): bg-accent, or bg-card again if it needs to read as a panel. Popovers/dropdowns/tooltips: bg-popover. Never use bg-muted as a page, section, or card background — muted is reserved for non-surface fills only (skeleton placeholders, disabled-state fills, inline code backgrounds), not for anything a user reads content on top of.

Paragraph text color, compulsory: use text-secondary for all paragraph text (body copy, section descriptions, card descriptions, and supporting text under headings). Never use text-muted-foreground for paragraphs; it is too low-contrast for reading text. Keep text-muted-foreground for small, low-priority text only: timestamps, metadata, captions, placeholders, helper and hint text, and disabled states. Use text-foreground for headings, titles, and anything that needs full emphasis. secondary is a text color only: never use it as a background (no bg-secondary). Order of emphasis: text-foreground (headings), then text-secondary (paragraphs), then text-muted-foreground (metadata and hints).
Status colors: success (positive/confirmation), warning (caution), info (neutral notice), destructive (danger/errors) — use these instead of ad-hoc green/yellow/blue/red.

Dark mode requires no extra work in generated code: the same class names resolve to the .dark palette automatically because the consumer's CSS defines both blocks. Do not write dark: variants for color — only use dark: for things the token system doesn't cover (rare).

Use the Card component, not a hand-rolled lookalike: this rule only applies once you've decided a group of content (a settings section, a stat/summary tile, a list item container, a form section, a feature block, etc.) needs a bounded/bordered panel treatment — it does not mean every grouping must be boxed (see the design rules' 'less UI is often better UI' guidance: whitespace-only grouping is often correct and a Card is often unnecessary). When a panel treatment is warranted, build it with <Card> — never a raw div styled to look like a card (e.g. bg-card border border-border rounded-lg p-4 by hand). <CardBody> is compulsory whenever the card has body content, not optional: <Card>'s own root element applies zero padding (only the border/background/radius) — all internal spacing lives in the sub-components via their shared padding context, so placing content directly as a child of <Card> without wrapping it in <CardBody> renders that content flush against the card's border with no padding, which visibly breaks the UI. <CardHeader> (title/description/icon/actions) and <CardFooter> (actions/meta) remain genuinely optional — include each only if that section is needed — but never skip <CardBody> when there is body content, and never place content as a direct child of <Card> itself.

Dropdown's trigger button: never call e.stopPropagation() (or preventDefault() for the same purpose) in an onClick you attach to the Dropdown's trigger element. The Dropdown component already stops propagation internally to manage its own open/close and outside-click behavior; adding it again on the consumer's trigger handler is redundant and can break the dropdown's outside-click / nested-dropdown / row-click interactions. If the trigger sits inside another clickable element (a table row, a card), rely on Dropdown's own handling instead of manually stopping propagation.

Do not overwrite a component's built-in design. Use each @neuctra/ui component's default classes/variants/sizes as-is by default — do not routinely pass a className that overrides its built-in spacing, radius, colors, or layout just to restyle it. Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`) when there's a real, specific need — the component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout/design, collide with a surrounding container, or the component itself has no prop for the needed variation — never as a routine styling habit or a stylistic preference.
antiAiLookRules: This section exists because AI-generated UI has recognizable tells. Read it before generating anything visual — the goal is UI indistinguishable from a deliberate human design pass, not a demo that screams 'built by an LLM'.

Brand effects are allowed, inside the theme, compulsory: gradients, glows, blur and animated backgrounds may be used to make a page feel branded, but every color in them must come from the theme tokens (var(--primary), var(--foreground), var(--background), var(--card), var(--border) and their /opacity variants, or color-mix() of them). Never introduce a color outside the theme for an effect: no from-purple-500 to-pink-500, no rainbow or multicolor gradients, no neon colors. Switching the theme must change every effect with it.

Gradients, restrained: use at most two theme colors per gradient (e.g. from-primary to-foreground, or primary fading to transparent). Allowed on: a few highlighted words in a heading (bg-clip-text), section and hero backgrounds, card edges, and thin divider lines. Not allowed on: buttons, body text, inputs, badges, or every heading on the page. At most one gradient heading per viewport.

No shadows on buttons and cards, compulsory: never add shadow-sm through shadow-2xl, drop-shadow, or any box-shadow to buttons, cards, panels, inputs, modals you build yourself, or any surface that holds content. Separate surfaces with border-border, a background change (bg-card vs bg-background) and spacing instead. Leave the built-in shadows of @neuctra/ui components (Modal, Drawer, Popover, Dropdown, Tooltip, Toast) exactly as they ship.

Glows are not shadows: a soft colored glow made from the primary token is allowed on small accents (a status dot, a step number, a progress bar, a timeline marker) and as a pointer-following light inside a card on hover. Keep it subtle (theme color at 10 to 30 percent opacity) and never use it on buttons, text or inputs.

Blur, in its place: backdrop-blur is allowed on sticky or fixed bars (navbar, tab bar, top bar) and on modal overlays, always with a mostly opaque token background (bg-background/75 or more). Large blurred blobs of the primary token (blur-[100px] or more, low opacity, pointer-events-none, aria-hidden) are allowed behind hero and section content. Never blur content the user reads, and never make a card see-through.

No blanket border-radius escalation — don't reach for rounded-2xl/rounded-3xl/rounded-full on every card, input, and button by default. Match the radius already used by the surrounding neuctra-ui components (rounded-md/rounded-lg/rounded-xl per component, see each component's own classes) instead of picking a bigger one because it 'looks more modern'.

Focus rings are for accessibility only: ring-* and focus-visible:ring-ring indicate keyboard focus. Never add a colored ring as a pointer-hover decoration on cards, buttons, or images. The only hover glow allowed is the soft pointer-following primary light inside a card described in the glow rule.

Animated backgrounds are allowed, compulsory conditions: they use only theme tokens, sit behind content (absolute, -z-10 or under a readable overlay, pointer-events-none, aria-hidden), stay low contrast so text keeps its contrast, run at most one per viewport, and stop when the user prefers reduced motion (MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" or a prefers-reduced-motion check). Never animate content itself, and never use flashing or fast loops.

Motion on interactive elements stays small: a hover lift of 1 to 4px or a press scale of about 0.97 is allowed on buttons, links and clickable cards. No scale-105 zooms, bouncing, floating icons or wobble. Idle animation is only for decorative backgrounds and live-status dots.

No emoji used as icons or bullet markers in generated UI (✨, 🚀, 💡, ✅ as list bullets, feature markers, or button icons). Use lucide-react icons — the same icon set every neuctra-ui component already uses — passed via each component's icon props (iconBefore, iconAfter, icon, etc.).

No 'icon in a colored circle badge' repeated on every single feature/stat/card by default (a bg-primary/10 rounded-full p-3 wrapper around every icon). Use it sparingly, only where the component's own design already calls for it — repeating the same decorative wrapper on every card in a grid is a generic-template tell.
No arbitrary one-off spacing/sizing values (p-[13px], gap-[7px], w-[327px]) — use the Tailwind spacing scale (p-3, gap-2, w-80, etc.) so spacing stays consistent with the rest of the design system.

Prefer information density and restraint over generic centered-hero-with-huge-padding layouts. Not every section needs max-w-7xl mx-auto text-center py-24 — match the density and layout the consumer's existing UI already uses.

Make every layout fully responsive by default — mobile, tablet, and desktop (sm:/md:/lg:/xl: breakpoints), stacking to a single column and adjusting spacing/type-scale at small widths. Never ship a fixed-width or desktop-only layout and call it done.

No em dashes (—), compulsory: never use an em dash in generated copy or UI text (headings, body copy, button labels, placeholder text). It's a recognizable AI-writing tell. Use a period, comma, colon, or restructure the sentence instead.

No over-effects: one decorative effect per element at most (a gradient OR a glow OR a hover lift), and the effects on one screen must share one color (the primary token). If an effect makes text harder to read or competes with the primary action, remove it.

Don't layer a separate leading-* utility (leading-relaxed, leading-normal, leading-tight, ...) on top of a text-size class (text-sm, text-base, text-lg, text-xl, ...) — Tailwind's text-size utilities already ship a paired line-height, so adding leading-* alongside one is redundant and can fight the intended rhythm. Only reach for leading-* when no text-size class is already setting one, and even then never leading-none/leading-tight on paragraph-length text. Letter-spacing: use tracking-tight on headings text-3xl and larger; leave everything smaller at the default (tracking-normal); only use tracking-wide for short uppercase labels (badges, eyebrow text, nav labels), and never tracking-wide on paragraph-length text.
Responsive, compulsory: every page must pass the Breakpoint Checklist in the design guide (360, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536px) with no horizontal scroll and touch targets of at least 44px.
One focal point per viewport: a single dominant element (usually the primary CTA or one bg-primary block) that the eye lands on first. Never several competing bg-primary blocks on one screen.
Use the fixed type scale from the design guide (Type Scale section). Never more than 4 text sizes on one screen, and keep paragraphs to max-w-prose or max-w-2xl.

The bar is branded and restrained: a page may have a signature look (gradient headline words, a glow, an animated background in the brand color), but it must still read well with every effect removed. Hierarchy, spacing and typography carry the design; effects only add the brand.

Decent, restrained design, compulsory: build UI that is decent and intentional, never over-designed. When unsure whether an effect (gradient, glow, blur, animation) is warranted on something you're authoring yourself, leave it out; shadows on content surfaces and colors outside the theme are never warranted. A flat, token-colored, appropriately-radiused, unshadowed, responsive surface is the correct default for most neuctra-ui components. Brand effects are added on purpose, only where the effect rules above allow them.

tokens.usage: Brand color: primary buttons, active states, links, focus accents.
Text/icons on top of bg-primary.
Page/app background.
Headings, titles, and anything that needs full emphasis.
Paragraph text: body copy, section/card descriptions, supporting text under headings. Text color only, never a background (no bg-secondary).
Subtle/secondary surfaces (skeletons, disabled fills, code blocks).
Small, low-priority text only: timestamps, metadata, captions, placeholders, helper/hint text, disabled text. Never paragraphs (use text-secondary).
Hover/active background for interactive rows and menu items.
Text on bg-accent.
Default border color for inputs, cards, dividers.
Form control backgrounds.
Focus ring color — always pair interactive elements with focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring.
Card / panel surfaces, distinct from the page background.
Text inside cards.
Dropdowns, popovers, tooltips, menus.
Text inside popovers/dropdowns.
Errors, delete/danger actions, invalid form states.
Text on bg-destructive.
Confirmation, online status, valid form states, positive metrics.
Text on bg-success.
Caution states, pending status, non-blocking alerts.
Text on bg-warning.
Neutral notices, informational banners/badges.
Text on bg-info.

note: Values shown are the CLI-generated defaults (npx @neuctra/ui-cli init). A consumer project may have redefined these hex values in its own CSS — the token NAMES and pairing rules are the stable contract; always prefer the class names over the hex values.

whatItDoes: Checks React (upgrades to >=18 if needed) and Tailwind CSS (upgrades to v4 if needed) — @neuctra/ui requires Tailwind v4 syntax (@theme, @source, @custom-variant).
Writes/updates the project's global CSS with the token blocks shown in this response (:root + .dark + @theme mapping) and the correct @source path for the project's own layout.

Generates a theme context file at src/contexts/ThemeContext.jsx (or .tsx if the project is TypeScript) exporting ThemeProvider and useTheme — handles localStorage persistence, system-preference detection with live updates, and avoids a flash of the wrong theme on load.
Wraps the app's entry point in <ThemeProvider>.
setup.whenToSuggestIt: If a project doesn't have @neuctra/ui installed yet, or has no theme token CSS / no ThemeContext, suggest running this command instead of hand-writing the CSS token blocks or a theme context from scratch — it is the maintained, correct source for both.
setup.manualSetupStillDocumented: If the consumer can't run a CLI (e.g. you're only shown existing code, not given shell access), the full manual step-by-step — including the exact ThemeContext implementation the CLI generates — is at the project's /docs/full-setup page (FullSetupDocPage) and is safe to reproduce by hand.

toastNote: @neuctra/ui's toast notification system is a standalone function, not hook-only: import { toast, ToastProvider } from '@neuctra/ui' and call toast(...) / toast.success(...) / toast.error(...) / toast.warning(...) / toast.info(...) / toast.loading(...) / toast.promise(...) from anywhere — event handlers, API clients, utility files — no useToast() hook required at the call site. Mount <ToastProvider> once near the app root so there is somewhere for toasts to render; mounting it more than once duplicates every toast. useToast() still exists for consumers who prefer a hook — it returns the identical global toast/dismiss, so both styles stay in sync. Use get-neuctra-ui-component with componentName "ToastProvider" for the full prop list (including position, one of top-left/top-center/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-center/bottom-right).
